tax.text: She called for repealing billionaire tax cuts to restore health care funding.
tax.quote: That means repealing billionaire tax cuts so we can restore funding for health care

wages.text: She voted for the Raise the Wage Act in 2019.
wages.quote: Jul 18, 2019, 12:01 PM | 116th Congress, 1st Session Vote Question: On Passage Raise the Wage Act Vote Type: Recorded Vote Status: Passed

trade.text: She said Congress should end the tariffs she argued raise prices and hurt U.S. businesses.
trade.quote: The most important thing the next Congress can do when it comes to U.S. trade policy is to end Donald Trump's and Jen Kiggans' cost-spiking tariffs

debt.text: She says Social Security and Medicare benefits should be protected without cuts.
debt.quote: Seniors who worked hard their entire lives and paid into Social Security and Medicare deserve to be secure in retirement with the peace of mind that their benefits will be there when they need them—without cuts.

housing.text: She called for making it easier to build new homes by cutting red tape.
housing.quote: We also need to ensure that at the federal, state, and local level we are making it as easy as possible to build new homes by cutting red tape

immigration.text: She supported stronger border security while also supporting a pathway to citizenship for people who follow the law.
immigration.quote: I was proud to support comprehensive efforts in Congress to deter illegal immigration and strengthen border security, while also providing a pathway to citizenship for those who follow our nation's laws.

guns.text: She said she would support gun safety measures including universal background checks.
guns.quote: In Congress, I will fight for commonsense gun safety measures, like universal background checks, to reduce preventable gun violence and keep our children safe.

abortion.text: She said she supports abortion rights and voted for federal legislation to codify abortion protections.
abortion.quote: I believe strongly in a woman's right to choose and make decisions for herself about her own body.

health.text: She called for protecting Medicaid, restoring ACA subsidies and expanding Medicare drug price negotiation.
health.quote: It means protecting Medicaid and restoring Obamacare subsidies so that working and middle class Virginians can afford high-quality, low-cost health insurance.

energy.text: In congressional testimony, she called for U.S. net greenhouse-gas emissions to reach zero by 2050.
energy.quote: We must reduce all net greenhouse gas emissions within the U.S. to zero by 2050 at the latest.

voting.text: She voted for the For the People Act and says she would continue to support it.
voting.quote: I was proud to support legislation that overturns the disastrous Citizens United decision when in Congress, and I will continue to fight for the For the People Act to restore fairness and power back to the people.

tax.text: She supported tax cuts and says she wants to keep taxes low for working families.
tax.quote: Jen also knows how important it is to keep taxes low for working families

debt.text: She says she will protect and preserve Social Security and Medicare benefits.
debt.quote: Jen is a fierce advocate for seniors and fights to protect and preserve Medicare and Social Security.

schools.text: She describes herself as a staunch advocate for school choice.
schools.quote: She has been a staunch advocate for school choice and prioritizes teaching our children “how to think”

safety.text: She says police should be fully funded and opposes efforts to defund them.
safety.quote: In the State Senate, Jen fought tirelessly for police officers, firefighters, emergency responders, and correctional officers to ensure they are fully funded

immigration.text: She supported increased border security funding and the Laken Riley Act to strengthen interior enforcement.
immigration.quote: She has also proudly voted in favor of bipartisan legislation and cosponsored the Laken Riley Act, which aims to strengthen interior enforcement

guns.text: She says she is a staunch defender of gun rights and supports policies that make it easier for law-abiding people to own guns.
guns.quote: Jen is a staunch defender of the Second Amendment who never compromises our right to bear arms.

abortion.text: She favors state-level abortion laws, opposes abortion up to birth, and supports exceptions for rape, incest, and the mother’s life.
abortion.quote: she believes abortion laws should be determined at the state level and is firmly opposed to the radical policies which would allow abortions up to the moment of birth.

gender.toward: rules based on sex at birth
gender.text: She has supported legislation to reserve women’s sports for biological women.
gender.quote: Jen has consistently voted to protect women’s sports and athletics for biological women since her days in the Virginia Senate.

health.text: She says she has worked to expand Medicare coverage and supported extending ACA premium tax credits.
health.quote: In Washington, Jen’s fought to expand medicare coverage and improve access to virtual healthcare.

energy.text: She supports an all-of-the-above approach, domestic production, and preservation of existing clean-energy tax credits.
energy.quote: We must put America first by prioritizing domestic energy production and protecting our existing clean energy tax credits.

voting.text: She supported photo ID requirements and other measures to tighten election rules.
voting.quote: She is committed to stopping voting irregularities, maintaining a photo ID requirement, preventing ballot harvesting

trade.text: He opposes broad executive-imposed tariffs but allows for narrowly tailored tariffs enacted by Congress.
trade.quote: I'm not against narrow tariffs Congress actually legislates. I'm against a President taxing every family by decree, changing the rate more than fifty times, and calling it a strategy.

debt.text: He criticizes adding to the national debt and says he would use honest budgets with tradeoffs to practice fiscal conservatism.
debt.quote: Voting to add more than $4 trillion to the debt while calling yourself a fiscal conservative is not a position; it is a performance. I will not perform fiscal conservatism. I will practice it: honest budgets, on time, with tradeoffs stated out loud.

housing.text: He supports increasing housing supply through faster permitting and updated zoning for starter homes and multifamily construction.
housing.quote: the fix starts with supply, not just subsidies. In Congress, I'd push for federal incentives that reward localities for cutting permitting timelines and updating outdated zoning

schools.text: He says school boards and educators should develop curriculum while Congress focuses on funding and civil-rights protections.
schools.quote: School boards together with educators should be developing curriculum, not individuals with an agenda, and not Washington.

immigration.text: He supports a path to citizenship while also calling for enforcement and accountability for people who commit crimes.
immigration.quote: A workable solution exists — a lawful pathway, real enforcement, and human dignity — and it requires the courage to negotiate rather than performance outrage.

guns.text: He supports the right to bear arms and also supports common-sense gun regulation.
guns.quote: The Second Amendment is the law of the land. Common-sense regulation is also the law of the land. Both are true simultaneously.

abortion.text: He says abortion is a personal decision for women and should not be dictated by government.
abortion.quote: I support a woman's right to choose, and while I hope she chooses life, it is her decision. Every circumstance is unique. She should be advised by her physician, not dictated to by the government.

health.text: He says he would oppose further Medicaid cuts that rural and coastal health facilities cannot absorb.
health.quote: I'd fix that math, push more of that fund straight to keeping doors open and staff paid, and fight further Medicaid cuts rural and coastal facilities can't absorb.

sources: wvtf.org · clerk.house.gov · elaineforcongress.com · giffords.org · congress.gov · jenforcongress.com · kiggans.house.gov · mattbakerindependent.com
